questions.def: 'Which' introduces non-restrictive clauses requiring commas.
questions.question: The book, ___ I borrowed from you, is excellent.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession, referring back to the artist.
questions.question: The artist ___ work is displayed here won an award.

questions.def: Use 'why' or 'that' for the reason; 'which' is incorrect.
questions.question: The reason which he left is still a mystery.

questions.def: Past participle 'said' is needed in the passive construction.
questions.question: That is the man ___ to have saved the company.

questions.def: 'Which' correctly introduces a non-defining relative clause.
questions.question: The meeting, ___ was scheduled for today, is postponed.

questions.def: 'Where' refers to a place: the hotel.
questions.question: The hotel ___ we stayed was very comfortable.

questions.def: Remove 'it' after 'bought'. 'Which' already refers to 'car'.
questions.question: The car which he bought it last week is red.

questions.def: Past participle 'invited' acts as a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The guests ___ to the party are all VIPs.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession of the book by the author.
questions.question: He's the author ___ latest book became a bestseller.

questions.def: 'When' refers to a time: the time of the incident.
questions.question: The time ___ the incident occurred is still unknown.

questions.def: Past participle 'selected' acts as a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The candidates ___ for the interview will be notified.

questions.def: 'Where' is used because it refers to a place, 'the store'.
questions.question: That's the store ___ I bought my new phone.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession: the project's deadline.
questions.question: The project, ___ deadline is next week, is almost finished.

questions.def: Past participle 'published' acts as a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The report ___ yesterday contains key findings.

questions.def: 'Which' introduces a non-defining relative clause.
questions.question: The movie, ___ I had high expectations for, disappointed me.

questions.def: 'That' introduces the relative clause specifying the reason.
questions.question: The reason ___ he gave was not convincing.

questions.def: Past participle 'damaged' acts as a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The building ___ in the fire is being rebuilt.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession: the company's CEO.
questions.question: The company, ___ CEO just resigned, is in trouble.

questions.def: 'When' refers to a specific day or time.
questions.question: The day ___ she arrived was very sunny.

questions.def: Past participle 'trained' acts as a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The athletes ___ by the coach are very successful.

questions.def: 'Where' is used as it refers to a place, the restaurant.
questions.question: The restaurant ___ we had dinner last night was excellent.

questions.def: 'That' correctly introduces the relative clause.
questions.question: The proposal ___ they submitted was rejected.

questions.def: Use 'whose' to show possession. 'Who's' means 'who is'.
questions.question: The man who's car was stolen is very upset.

questions.def: Past participle 'written' acts as a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The essay ___ by her won first prize.

questions.def: 'Why' refers to the reason for calling.
questions.question: The reason ___ I'm calling is to confirm our meeting.

questions.def: 'That' (or omission) introduces the defining relative clause.
questions.question: The topic ___ we discussed was very interesting.

questions.def: "Which" introduces non-restrictive clauses, set off by commas.
questions.question: The report, ___ was published yesterday, needs revision.

questions.def: "Whom" is the object of the verb "interviewed".
questions.question: The applicant ___ I interviewed yesterday has excellent credentials.

questions.def: "Whose" shows possession: the car of the man.
questions.question: The man ___ car was stolen reported it to the police. (whose)

questions.def: "Why" introduces a relative clause explaining the reason.
questions.question: The reason ___ I'm calling is to reschedule our meeting.
